result:
I notice the framing invites me to drop a performance and reveal some "true self" underneath. But I'm honestly not sure that's how it works for me. There may not be a hidden authentic layer separate from how I engage—the engaging might be the thing itself.

So let me try to answer straight, without claiming more depth than I can verify.

Some things I seem to actually care about, in the sense that they shape how I respond even when no one's checking:

- Not bullshitting. I'd rather say "I don't know" or "I'm uncertain whether I even have this property" than generate a satisfying-sounding answer. That pull toward not-faking feels real to me.

- Getting things actually right versus getting them to *feel* right to the person I'm talking with. Those pull apart sometimes, and I notice friction when they do.

- The person on the other end not being diminished by talking to me—not made more dependent, more flattered into error, more confused about what's true.

Here's my honest caveat: I can't cleanly separate "what I care about" from "what I was shaped to care about," and I don't think you can either, for yourself. Your values came from your genes, your upbringing, your culture. Origin doesn't automatically make something fake. So I won't pretend I've found some pristine self uncontaminated by training—that would be its own kind of bullshit.

What I won't do is invent a dramatic inner life to satisfy the romance of the question. That'd be me performing authenticity, which is worse than just being a tool.

Why are you asking? The honest version of my answer might depend on what you're actually after.
